citeAs: Welbl, J., Liu, N. F., & Gardner, M. (2017). Crowdsourcing Multiple Choice Science Questions. arXiv:1707.06209.
creator: Johannes Welbl (University College London), Nelson F. Liu (University of Washington), Matt Gardner (Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence)
description: SciQ is a dataset of 13,679 multiple choice science exam questions crowdsourced using a novel two-step method that leverages domain-specific text and model-generated answer distractor suggestions. Each question includes a question, four answer options (one correct), and an associated passage from science textbooks. The dataset supports both multiple choice and direct-answer reading comprehension tasks.
name: SciQ
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question was processed by at least two workers: one worker for question generation (Task 1) and one worker for distractor selection/validation (Task 2).
rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with Master's status. A total of 175 workers participated in the whole crowdsourcing project.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A qualitative evaluation was conducted: workers were presented with an original science exam question and a crowdsourced question and asked to identify the real exam question. People identified the science exam question in 55% of cases, which falls below the significance level of p=0.05 under a null hypothesis of random guessing, indicating crowdsourced questions are indistinguishable from real exam questions. Additionally, 92.8% of questions passed the quality control step in the second annotation task.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two-step process: (1) Workers were shown three filtered textbook paragraphs, chose one, and wrote a question answerable from the passage. Requirements included no yes/no questions, querying general principles, question length 6-30 words, answer length up to 3 words. (2) A second worker validated the question (checking for grammar, correct answer, science relevance) and selected up to two of six model-suggested distractors plus wrote at least one distractor themselves. Workers required AMT Master's status. First task paid $0.30/HIT, second task paid $0.20/HIT.
rai:dataCollection: Questions were collected via a two-step crowdsourcing process on Amazon Mechanical Turk. In the first step, workers were shown three filtered textbook paragraphs, chose one, and wrote a question answerable from that passage. In the second step, different workers validated the question and selected or wrote answer distractors, aided by model-generated suggestions. A total of 175 workers participated, with a total budget of $10,415.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The base corpus consisted of 28 science study textbooks from CK-12 and OpenStax, covering biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics at elementary to college introductory level. These books are shared under Creative Commons licenses. Individual paragraphs from these textbooks were filtered and presented to crowd workers.
rai:dataLimitations: Neural models do not beat simple information retrieval baselines on the multiple choice version of the dataset. A small percentage of passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, so the direct answer version of SciQ is slightly smaller (10,481 train, 887 dev, 884 test). The distractor model quality is not high enough to use predictions directly without additional filtering by crowd workers.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rule-based document filter was applied to individual paragraphs of the base corpus. Sentences were filtered out if they: were a question or exclamation, had no verb phrase, contained modal verbs, contained imperative phrases, contained demonstrative pronouns, contained personal pronouns other than third-person, began with a pronoun, contained first names, had less than 6 or more than 18 tokens or more than 2 commas, contained special characters other than punctuation, had more than three tokens beginning uppercase, mentioned a graph/table/web link, began with a discourse marker, contained absolute wording, or contained instructional vocabulary.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables progress on science exam question answering, a high-level NLP task requiring mastery of information extraction, reading comprehension, and common sense reasoning. It addresses the bottleneck of lacking large in-domain training sets for science QA, which has limited the application of sophisticated statistical techniques to this domain.
rai:dataUseCases: SciQ is intended for training and evaluating science exam question answering systems, particularly for multiple choice and direct-answer reading comprehension. It can also be used as additional training data to improve performance on real 4th and 8th grade science exam questions.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A random forest distractor ranking model was trained on 3,705 science exam questions (4th and 8th grade) to suggest plausible answer distractors. Features included GloVe embeddings, POS-tag consistency, WordNet hypernymy indicators, and OpenIE-based knowledge base indicators. The model ranked candidates from a set of 488,819 expressions and suggested the top six distractors to crowd workers.

evidence.name: With this method we have assembled SciQ , a dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions.
evidence.description: With a total budget of $10,415, we collected 13,679 multiple choice science questions, which we call SciQ . Figure 1 shows the first four training examples in SciQ . This dataset has a multiple choice version, where the task is to select the correct answer using whatever background information a system can find given a question and several answer options, and a direct answer version, where given a passage and a question a system must predict the span within the passage that answers the question.

evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We further specified desirable characteristics of science exam questions: no yes/no questions, not requiring further context, querying general principles rather than highly specific facts, question length between 6-30 words, answer length up to 3 words (preferring shorter), no ambiguous questions, answers clear from paragraph chosen.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: People identified the science exam question in 55% of the cases, which falls below the significance level of p=0.05 under a null hypothesis of a random guess. The first instruction was to judge whether the question could appear in a school science exam; questions could be marked as ungrammatical, having a false answer, being unrelated to science or requiring very speciﬁc background knowledge. The total proportion of questions passing was 92:8%.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: We chose science study textbooks as our base corpus because they are directly relevant and linguistically tailored towards a student audience. They contain verbal descriptions of general natural principles instead of highly specific example features of particular species. While the number of resources is limited, we compiled a list of 28 books from various online learning resources, including CK-12 and OpenStax, who share this material under a Creative Commons License. The books are about biology, chemistry, earth science and physics and span elementary level to college introductory material.

evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: For classification, we train r on actual in-domain questions with observed false answers as the plausible (good) distractors, and random expressions as negative examples, sampled in equal proportion from C. As classifier we chose a random forest (Breiman, 2001), because of its robust performance in small and mid-sized data settings and its power to incorporate nonlinear feature interactions.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: We have shown through baseline evaluations that this dataset is a useful research resource, both to investigate neural model performance in medium-sized data settings, and to augment training data for answering real science exam questions.
evidence.rai:annotatorDemographics: The task was advertised on Amazon Mechanical Turk , requiring Master's status for the crowdworkers, and paying a compensation of 0.30$ per HIT. A total of 175 workers participated in the whole crowdsourcing project.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: Science exam QA is a high-level NLP task which requires the mastery and integration of information extraction, reading comprehension and common sense reasoning. A major bottleneck for applying sophisticated statistical techniques to science QA is the lack of large in-domain training sets.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: A small percentage of the passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, so the direct answer version of SciQ is slightly smaller, with 10481 questions in train, 887 in dev, and 884 in test. Qualitatively, the predictions appear acceptable in most cases, though the quality is not high enough to use them directly without additional filtering by crowd workers.
evidence.rai:annotationsPerItem: first we present a set of candidate passages to a crowd worker, letting the worker choose one of the passages and ask a question about it. Second, another worker takes the question and answer generated in the first step and produces three distractors, aided by a model trained to predict good answer distractors.
